newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan stocks stay firm on blue chip demand.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan stocks stay firm on blue chip demand.

text.p: Sri Lankan stocks were firmer at mid-morning on buying of blue chips and plantation shares, brokes said.
The all share index was 1.03 points higher at 560.04 at mid-morning break. Seylan Bank rose 25 local cents to 23.75 and Dipped Products, a rubber glove manufacturer, gained four rupees to 80.
"There is local and foreign buying for a range of stocks but sellers are seeking at least 10 percent over current market levels," said Shanil Perera of brokerage Lanka Securities.

Blue chips Hayleys, John Keells Holdings and Aitken Spence, development finance institutions of NDB and DFCC, Commercial Bank, Seylan Bank, Kotagala Plantations, Kegalle Plantations and Horana Plantations, were among favoured stocks, brokers said.
"Foreign buyers want quantities worth at least $50,000. But even at premiums of five percent to a market you cannot get sellers to loosen up," said one broker.
Turnover was a thin 4.71 million rupees on 442,511 shares.
